findings.where: First screen, Mark's photograph (desktop right half; phone, the head above the heading)
findings.fault: The photo has been cut out of its event and blown up into a huge close-up of a head on flat navy, cropped at the chest. The lectern, the backdrop and every sign of a talk are gone, so this is no longer 'Mark at work' or 'Mark speaking'. On the overview the face outweighs everything else and reads like a political campaign poster. On the phone it reads as a floating head.
findings.who_objects: A senior development-bank official looking for counsel, who expects the quiet standing of a legal advisor and reads a giant tight portrait as self-promotion. The founder would also object, because v7's lever (Mark seen at work at a real event) has turned into v6's portrait.

findings.where: First screen, the edge of the cut-out photograph: hair, left ear and the left shoulder line against the slate (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The keyed edge is ragged and haloed. You can see where the purple backdrop was cut away around the hair and the shoulder, so the 'graded' photo looks like a rough cut-out pasted onto the colour.
findings.who_objects: The visiting official, who takes a visibly rough cut-out on the very first screen as a cheap, home-made finish for someone advising governments.

findings.where: First screen, the heading and the lede under it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Nothing on the first screen says Mark is a lawyer or drafts laws. The heading is about PPPs in general, and the lede says he advises 'on infrastructure… Public-Private Partnerships'. Words like law, legal and legislation appear only far below, in the article specimen.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who came for an independent legal advisor on a PPP law. They cannot tell from the first screen whether Mark is legal counsel or a financial or transaction advisor. The founder would also object, because the brief asks the look to reflect 'law, PPP and advice to governments'.

findings.where: First screen, around the 'Write to me directly' action
findings.fault: Next to the one action there is nothing a visitor can check: no region of his work, no named body that asked for his advice, and no recent talk or venue. The only evidence before the contact is an opinion and a face.
findings.who_objects: A procurement-minded official who judges advisors by relevant work and region. Before writing, they need some sign that Mark has done this kind of work for bodies like theirs.

findings.fault: There are two nav items for what a visitor sees as the same kind of thing, his writing. The difference between an 'article' and a 'blog' post is not clear, and the article specimen itself is labelled 'Blog No. 8'.
findings.who_objects: The visitor who wants his writing on PPP law and has to guess which of the two items holds it.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process… · Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' row after the article
findings.fault: The row has no heading or label saying what it is (a related talk? an attachment?). It also announces itself as a direct PDF download with a download arrow, rather than leading to the talk's own page.
findings.who_objects: A reader who finishes the article, meets an unrelated lecture title with no explanation, and is sent straight into a file rather than a page they can judge first.

findings.where: Article specimen, the three-item list's numerals (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The list numbers are in the link blue. The page's own note says 'blue only where something can be clicked', so these static numerals borrow the colour kept for links.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader who has learned that blue means a link on this site and finds the numbers do nothing. Angélique would object too, as she would inherit a colour rule the page itself breaks.

findings.where: First screen header, the MMM Infra mark and wordmark reversed to warm white
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured to white for the dark hero. Mark does not hold a white version of the logo, and no approval for one is recorded.
findings.who_objects: Mark, as owner of the logo, whose permission a new logo version needs.

findings.fault: The display title appears to use a straight apostrophe, while the subhead and quotations further down use curly quotes. At this size the difference shows.
findings.who_objects: A reader with an eye for typesetting, for whom a straight tick in a large serif title undercuts the 'legal journal' care the page aims at.
